core_obligations: Let Y be a connected component of the reduced geometric base change of X and apply the algebraically closed case to Y, noting that the irreducible components of the two base changes agree (proof lines 5363-5377).

Derive the contrapositive: if O(X)^*/k^* is not finitely generated, then there is f in O(X) outside k whose image in O(Y) lies in the algebraic closure; such f is algebraic and hence integral over k, so condition (1) rules it out (proof lines 5378-5383).

Show that (2) implies (1): a k-rational point e : Spec(k) -> X gives a section of k -> O(X), and the restriction of this section to the integral closure k' is a field map k' -> k over k, forcing k' = k (proof lines 5387-5394 and following).
Show that (3) implies (1), completing the proof up to line 5403 (remaining lines of the proof).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the algebraically closed case via a geometric connected component.
Produce a non-constant integral element when finite generation fails.
Verify that each of the three hypotheses excludes that possibility.
difficulty_reason: The proposition proves finite generation of O(X)^*/k^* for a connected reduced locally finite type scheme with finitely many irreducible components, provided at least one of three conditions holds: the integral closure of k in the global sections is k, X has a k-rational point, or X is geometrically integral. The proof passes to a connected component Y of the reduced geometric base change, applies the algebraically closed case to Y, and uses it to produce, under the failure of finite generation, an element f of O(X) not in k whose image under O(X) -> O(Y) lies in the algebraic closure (proof lines 5363-5383). It then shows that conditions (2) and (3) each imply condition (1): a k-rational point gives a section of the inclusion k -> O(X), forcing the integral closure to be k, and geometric integrality gives the same conclusion through the integral closure being a field (proof lines 5384-5403). H3: the passage to the geometric base change and the comparison of the three hypotheses is independent work.
